quandoUsar: Async actions that should show progress and confirmation on the button itself: save draft, publish, sync.
When you want the pending and done states managed by the component from a single `onAction` function.
quandoEvitar: Use `button` when you need variants, sizes, or your own icon: here the look is fixed, filled, with an arrow on the right.
Use `action-swap` when the button toggles between states that persist, like Follow and Following, or needs a tone and icon per state.
Use `confirm-morph` or `hold-to-confirm` when the action is destructive and needs confirmation before it runs.

teclado.acao: Trigger `onAction`; while the action is pending, further activations are ignored.

acessibilidade: It is a native `<button>` with `type="button"` by default; while pending, it gets `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` instead of `disabled`, so focus is not lost mid-action.
The animated text and the icons are `aria-hidden`: the screen reader gets the fixed `label` and a `role="status"` that announces `pendingLabel` and then `successLabel`.
`pendingLabel` and `successLabel` default to English (“Saving” and “Saved”); pass both in the interface language.
movimento: The label swaps with a short fade (the new one rises 2 px) and the button width follows the text with a spring with no overshoot.
The arrow exits to the right when the action starts, gives way to a spinner and then to a checkmark that draws itself; on return to rest, the arrow enters from the left.
With “reduce motion”, the label swaps instantly, the icons only fade, the width jumps, the checkmark appears already drawn, and the spinner does not spin.
responsivo: The label does not wrap and the width changes with each state; in tight rows, use text of similar length in `label`, `pendingLabel`, and `successLabel` so neighbors do not shift.
desempenho: Each button keeps a `ResizeObserver` to measure the label and a timer to return to rest; avoid hundreds of them in a long list.
notasIA: The action goes in `onAction` (there is no `onClick`): return a Promise so the pending state lasts while it runs, and reject it to signal failure.
On failure the button returns to rest with no message and calls `onActionError`; show the error yourself, for example with `toast`.
`resetAfterMs` (default 2400) sets how long the done state stays visible; with `0` it stays until the next click.
